examples.solution_text:
(a) Follow 10 am up to the line, then read across to the water-level axis: $20\text{ cm}$.

(b) The line is horizontal from 10 am to 11 am, so the level stayed unchanged then.

(c) The level increased from 9 am to 10 am, stayed unchanged until 11 am, increased until noon, then decreased until 1 pm.

(d) Read the two levels: $25\text{ cm}$ at noon and $15\text{ cm}$ at 1 pm.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}25-15\\&=10\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$
The level decreased by $10\text{ cm}$.
From noon to 1 pm. This is the steepest segment, so it represents the fastest travel. A downward segment represents travelling towards home.

examples.derivation: The plotted levels at 9 am, 10 am, 11 am, noon and 1 pm are 10, 20, 20, 25 and 15 cm. Thus the 10 am reading is 20 cm; the horizontal interval is 10–11 am; successive changes are increase, unchanged, increase and decrease. The final decrease is 25−15=10 cm. These methods match the supplied reading, horizontal-segment, trend and difference tasks. The subtraction has the required phantom equals gutter.

The segment connects 15°C at 10 am to 25°C at 11 am. At the halfway time, 10:30 am, its height is 20°C. The solution guides meet at (1.5,20), matching the graph and answer. This follows the supplied room-temperature example's graphical estimation method with different values; the derived guides appear only in the solution.

All four intervals last one hour. Their absolute distance changes are 10, 0, 15 and 25 km, independently confirming that noon–1 pm is the steepest and fastest segment. Its falling direction represents returning towards home. The student solution correctly uses steepness without calculations, as requested in the supplied Mastery question 11d.
